purpose: Vessels and nerves whose vertices inside a bone mesh are anatomical (a canal, foramen, groove or notch the bone mesh does not model as a hole) and must NOT be pushed out by scripts/anatomy/q357/conform_in_bone_q357.py. 'allow': the passage is real, the vertices stay. 'unsure': not settled from the books checked; the structure stays and is listed. Everything else found inside a bone is treated as a registration error and conformed under guards.
matching: ids: regex fullmatched against the mesh id with the leading 'zan_' and a trailing side suffix ('_l' / '_r') removed; bones: regex fullmatched against the bone key of scripts/anatomy/q241/model.bone_key with its side suffix removed. Per (structure, bone) pair: a structure can be allowed in one bone and conformed out of another.
use_rule: Knowledge only: facts with book and printed page; no prose or figures copied; the PDFs stay outside the repo (docs/Q348_reference_pass.md).

sources.Y: Sontakke YA. Textbook of Human Anatomy with Color Atlas and Clinical Integration, Vol. 5 Head, Neck and Face (+ Vol. 6 Brain). 1st e-book ed., CBS Publishers, New Delhi, 2023. Printed pages.
sources.M: Noor MA. Mannan's Regional Dissection and Surface Anatomy, 14th ed., Jaypee Brothers, New Delhi, 2017, ISBN 978-93-86322-11-1. Printed pages.
sources.G: Gray's Atlas of Anatomy (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell et al.), Churchill Livingstone / Elsevier; edition and year not in the owner's scan. Printed page numbers of the labelled plates.

allow.passage: carotid canal through the petrous temporal bone, across the foramen lacerum, then in the carotid groove on the side of the sphenoid body
foramen spinosum (middle meningeal artery) and foramen ovale (accessory meningeal branch); the middle meningeal vessels groove the inner surface of the squamous temporal and parietal bones
foramen rotundum, then the infraorbital groove and canal of the maxilla; palatine branches in the greater and lesser palatine canals
infraorbital groove and canal (with the infraorbital nerve) to the infraorbital foramen
mandibular foramen and mandibular canal (inferior alveolar nerve and vessels) to the mental foramen
alveolar canals on the infratemporal surface of the maxilla (posterior superior alveolar nerve and vessels)
greater (pterygopalatine) palatine canal and greater / lesser palatine foramina
sphenopalatine foramen (between the orbital and sphenoidal processes of the palatine bone and the sphenoid body) into the nasal cavity
cribriform plate (olfactory nerve; anterior ethmoidal nerve and vessels) and the anterior / posterior ethmoidal canals
superior orbital fissure between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid
internal auditory meatus, facial canal of the petrous temporal bone, stylomastoid foramen; the chorda tympani leaves the facial canal through the middle ear and its anterior canaliculus
jugular foramen between the petrous temporal and the occipital bone (cranial nerves IX, X, XI, the inferior petrosal and sigmoid sinuses becoming the internal jugular vein)
hypoglossal canal of the occipital bone
foramen magnum (vertebral arteries, spinal roots of the accessory nerve)
foramina transversaria of the cervical vertebrae

the sinuses lie in grooves on the inner surface of the skull (sagittal sulcus, grooves for the transverse, sigmoid and superior petrosal sinuses, internal occipital crest) that the bone meshes do not model
cavernous and intercavernous sinuses on the body of the sphenoid around the sella; basilar venous plexus on the clivus
obturator canal (obturator groove of the pubis completed by the obturator membrane)
greater sciatic foramen above / below the piriformis, round the ischial spine, lesser sciatic foramen and pudendal canal (between bone and ligament: the bone mesh forms one wall of the opening)
the sacral plexus is formed by anterior rami that leave the sacrum through the anterior (pelvic) sacral foramina, as spinal nerves leave through the intervertebral foramina
intervertebral foramina
radial (spiral) groove on the back of the humerus (radial nerve with the profunda brachii vessels and their collateral branches)
costal groove on the lower inner border of each rib (intercostal vein, artery and nerve)
groove for the subclavian artery on the upper surface of the first rib
nutrient foramen and canal of the bone

unsure.reason: its third part enters the pterygopalatine fossa through the pterygomaxillary fissure, a narrow cleft between the maxilla and the pterygoid process that the bone meshes may close; registration error and real course cannot be told apart here
its meningeal branches enter the skull through the foramen lacerum, jugular foramen and hypoglossal canal; which part of the mesh is the intracranial branch is not resolvable
climbs the clivus in the dura to the petrous apex before the cavernous sinus; not confirmed in the books checked whether the clivus mesh should clear it
runs under the orbital roof to the superior orbital fissure; 1-2 mm into the frontal orbital plate may be the thin orbital roof itself
dental and incisive branches enter the roots of the lower teeth at their apical foramina; the tooth meshes have no root canals, so a correct course and a registration error look the same
the septal branches end at the incisive canal of the maxilla; which part of the mesh lies in the canal is not resolvable

out_of_scope.reason: brain and ear parts that the loader files on the nerve layer; not vessels or nerves, not part of this round (the auditory tube's bony part and the tympanic membrane do sit in the temporal bone)
